properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:52PM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides in the late
mornings.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
late mornings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the warned area should prepare for rising
water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property. High tides each day will occur in the late morning.
Observed high tides are 1.5 to 1.7 feet above astronomical
tide predictions.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 PM MDT Monday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 PM MDT Monday was 6.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Tuesday morning and continue falling to 4.5 feet through
Wednesday.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.5
feet on 08/06/2006.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
Areas of fog will continue overnight over most of northeastern
Wyoming and western South Dakota.

Patchy dense fog will occur through sunrise. With temperatures
near freezing, elevated surfaces such as overpasses and bridges
may become slick.

Motorists should expect rapidly changing visibility, down to near
zero at times. Remember to use your low beam headlights in fog,
slow down, and provide plenty of braking distance between yourself
and any vehicles in front of you.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 8:59PM PDT until October 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the

erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

astronomical projections. The highest tides will be through
Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal Flood
Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf develops.

Thursday.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:31PM CDT until October 27 at 3:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge affecting
Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Presidio Vehicle Bridge.

* WHEN...From this evening to Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, after which the
flood plain between the levees begins to flood.  No damage is
expected. At 15.5 feet, the river reaches minor flood stage, and
flooding between the levees occurs.  No damage to structures is
expected. At 20.0 feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage,
inundating the plain between the levees.  Erosion of the levees is
likely.  Water may seep through the levees, flooding adjacent
farmland. At 22.9 feet, the river reaches major flood stage.  While
water remains between the levees at Presidio, areas downstream may
experience significant flooding.  FM 170 downstream of Presidio
will flood in low spots.  Farmland along the river will be
inundated. At 25.0 feet, the river remains between the levees at
Presidio, although continued flows at this level could cause damage
to the levees.  FM 170 downstream will likely be flooded and
impassable in spots.  Farmland around the river will continue to
inundate. At 25.8 feet, the river reaches record stage for the
period of record (1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but
the exact stage is unknown.  FM 170 will be flooded downstream of
Presidio.  Farmland around the river will remain inundated. At 28.2
feet, the river reaches record stage for the period of record
(1978).  A higher stage was reached in 1932, but the exact stage is
unknown.  FM 170 remains flooded downstream of Presidio.  Farmland
adjacent to the river remains inundated. At 30.0 feet, The top of
the levee is reached, and water will begin to overtop the levees.
Major flooding of Presidio and surrounding farmland is likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM CDT Monday the stage was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM CDT Monday was 42.1 feet (12.8 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 4.1 feet (1.2
meters) Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet (4.7 meters).
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 26 at 3:30PM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state from the southwest will bring
abundant tropical moisture late Tuesday through at least Wednesday
night. Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce
flash flooding, and while the greatest flood threat will be focused
over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
are expected to develop on Tuesday and continue through Wednesday
night as a trough moves over the state. While the greatest flood
threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are
at risk.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

tidal waterways (9.6 to 9.8 feet Mean Lower Low Water at Fort
Pulaski).

Liberty and Coastal McIntosh Counties. In South Carolina,
Beaufort and Coastal Jasper Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Tuesday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to noon EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater inundation will impact some roads. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 9:15 AM Tuesday at
Fort Pulaski. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:20PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to remain in Moderate Flood Stage, perhaps beginning a
slow decline late week into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Monday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Monday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Socorro, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 7:14PM MDT until October 30 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, old Highway 60 bridge is overtopped. At
23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco between
interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are being
flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been this
high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also be
flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Monday the stage was 24.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:00 PM MDT Monday was 24.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually fall into minor
flood stage early Tuesday morning, then rise again to 21.8 feet
Wednesday morning before falling below flood stage Thursday.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon MDT.

* WHAT...High flow is traveling down the Upper Purgatoire from recent
rains, and may lead to flooding near Las Animas.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...From late tonight to late Wednesday night.

- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 10.5 feet tomorrow evening.
It will then fall below flood stage Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.5
feet on 08/19/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 715 AM MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 8:29AM MDT until October 27 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring or expected to
begin shortly. The crest will occur around Aneth, Montezuma Creek
and Bluff this afternoon and evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 823 AM MDT, - At 7:30 AM MDT Monday the stage was 24.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM MDT Monday was 24.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 31.0 feet
late this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 32.0
feet on 09/10/1927.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

into the weekend. Winds and seas will sharply increase starting early
Friday ahead of the approaching typhoon, quickly exceeding hazardous
levels to small craft early on Friday. Seas of 10 to 15 feet are
expected to develop in the coastal of Tinian and Saipan. Although,
sustained winds are not expected to reach tropical-storm force at
this time, tropical-storm force gusts are possible. Mariners are
urged to remain weather aware over the coming days.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 26 at 3:22AM EDT until October 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to
8 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to possibly major
flooding around times of high tide. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor flooding expected around times of high tide.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 11 AM EDT Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM Tuesday to 2 AM EDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 9:00AM MDT until October 27 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall which occurred over
the last couple of days is expected or ongoing.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Alamosa County in southeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will occur in low-lying and flood-prone
locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 852 AM MDT, flooding was occurring along the Rio Grande River
in low lying and agricultural areas. This high water is due to
all of the heavy rain which occurred over the last couple of
days.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include low lying
areas in parts of Alamosa and parts of Conejos counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.
